root_cause.text: In the memory management subsystem, the `do_swap_page` function spins indefinitely when failing to acquire a device-private folio lock, starving the CPU required by the lock holder to execute pending work and release the resource.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states that if `folio_trylock()` fails in `do_swap_page`, "the function will spin until it succeeds grabbing the lock," which can starve a work item scheduled on the same CPU that the lock holder depends on to proceed; the patch resolves this by replacing the spin behavior with a call to `softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked()` in `mm/memory.c` to wait for the folio to be unlocked.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The `do_swap_page()` function in the memory management subsystem causes a livelock by busy-spinning when `folio_trylock()` fails to acquire a device-private folio lock, starving the CPU-bound work items required by the lock holder to release the lock.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch modifies `mm/memory.c` to replace the immediate unlock/return path with `softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked()`, and the CVE description identifies the scenario where spinning prevents `lru_add_drain_all()` work items from completing on the same CPU.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement attempts to acquire the device-private folio lock using trylock_page(). When this fails (returns false), the code falls through to an else branch that calls softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked(), which can spin indefinitely waiting for the lock. This indefinite spinning starves the CPU needed by the lock holder to complete their work and release the resource, creating the starvation vulnerability described in the root cause.

This else branch executes when trylock_page() fails to acquire the device-private folio lock. It calls softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked() which implements the waiting logic that can spin indefinitely without proper timeout or yield mechanisms. This is the core mechanism causing CPU starvation as the lock holder cannot make progress while the current thread holds CPU cycles in an indefinite spin loop.
